record.trigger: A component requirement combines mode-qualified threshold activation, an interior reset band, and language such as 'hold' or 'retain' the command within hysteresis bands.
record.principle: Preserve mode guards, exact interval boundaries, and command history together when translating a hysteresis requirement across architecture, contract, implementation, proof, tests, and repair.
record.semantic_choice: Interpret 'below' and 'above' as strict comparisons, 'hold' as equality to the previously emitted command, and the reset band as inclusive at its stated endpoints. Each mode-qualified obligation applies only in that mode; normal threshold behavior must not override initialization or failure behavior.
record.structural_placement: The output-producing thread owns the command and its history. In the observed example this is Manage_Alarm_i, whose GUMBO block owns alarm_control and declares lastCmd. Manage_Alarm_Process_i and Monitor_Temperature_i route existing ports; interface validation and monitor-mode production remain with their existing owners.
record.repair_gate: Proposed: accept a repair only after showing that it preserves every original case implication, initialization, history semantics, interval endpoints, mode behavior, and source interface. A missing state initialization/update or incompatible numeric encoding must be resolved explicitly before applying the pattern. Do not weaken guards, add a sensor-validity guard, or alter mode behavior merely to satisfy an implementation or proof.
prerequisites: The target has explicitly corresponding mode-gated activation, hold, and reset requirements; resemblance to a generic range controller is insufficient.
Existing port types, enum literals, connections, ownership, dispatch settings, and contract obligations are available as the baseline.
Temperature encoding, precision, units, and arithmetic semantics are established; all threshold computations are representable.
The threshold provider has a documented obligation ensuring L <= U. Any stronger range-width requirement must be justified separately.
The target supplies or can internally realize a previous-command state initialized consistently with the initial command, without changing interfaces.
exclusions: Stateless range checks or requirements that switch off throughout the closed interval [L,U].
Timeouts, debounce, trend detection, or continuous-time response guarantees.
Inferring sensor-invalid behavior absent from the alarm cases.
Inferring a physical buzzer, light, or other operator-interface design.
Applying the pattern to the mode-manager state machine or failure detector without corresponding hysteresis requirements.

parameters.name: m, x, L, U
parameters.role: Current mode, sampled temperature, lower bound, and upper bound
parameters.constraints: Bind to existing inputs and their numeric representation; retain the source mode enum and L <= U.

parameters.name: h
parameters.constraints: Positive and representable in the same numeric scale as x, L, and U. The example uses 1 [s32]; this syntax alone does not establish a physical temperature unit.

parameters.name: y, p
parameters.role: Emitted command and previous emitted command
parameters.constraints: Use the existing command type. In the example On is encoded by On_Off.Onn and Off by On_Off.Off; p is internal history.

preserved_obligations: Preserve all existing source interfaces, including names, directions, types, enum encodings, and connections; retain existing scheduling declarations.
Preserve initial Off, INIT-to-Off, FAILED-to-On, strict out-of-range activation, both hysteresis hold cases, and inclusive reset behavior.
Implementation obligation, proposed: initialize p to Off; on each dispatch compute y using the pre-dispatch p and current inputs, emit y, and update p to y for the next dispatch.

Proof obligation, proposed: establish initialization, preservation of the history invariant, and refinement of every applicable case. Check case coverage and overlapping-case consistency under the documented numeric and range assumptions.

Testing obligation, proposed: exercise every mode, activation below L and above U, all four endpoints L, L+h, U-h, U, and reachable hold cases with both previous command values. Include sequences entering a hold band from activation and reset regions.
Testing obligation, proposed: exercise narrow ordered ranges where hold bands overlap or the reset band is empty; use the conjunction of applicable case implications as the oracle.

Deployment obligation, proposed: preserve the existing component wiring and dispatch configuration and check that internal history persists across dispatches and resets consistently with initialization.

Repair obligation, proposed: rerun affected proof and behavioral checks after changes to comparisons, arithmetic, mode mapping, state updates, or generated implementation, without discarding unrelated baseline obligations.

counterexample.scenario: In NORMAL mode, let L=10, U=20, h=1 and x=10 in a compatible numeric encoding. Compare executions whose previous commands are On and Off.
counterexample.expected_difference: The scoped rule holds On in the first execution and Off in the second. A superficially similar requirement saying 'turn off whenever L <= x <= U' produces Off in both and must not receive this rule.

record.notes: Observed: Manage_Alarm_i declares lastCmd and the initialization and mode/interval cases described here; its supplied contract does not explicitly initialize or update lastCmd. The context discusses documenting environmental types, ranges, precision, units, ownership, and requirement traceability. Proposed: operational history handling and implementation/proof/testing/deployment/repair obligations are inferred requirements for applying this rule, not observed implementation results. No validation implementation or held-out component is supplied. Source references and hashes are left for the trusted controller.
source_english_patterns: If mode NORMAL and current temperature is below alarm range then alarm control is On
If mode NORMAL and current temperature is inside the lower hysteresis band then hold alarm control
If mode NORMAL and current temperature is inside the reset band then alarm control is Off
positive_paraphrases: During normal operation, activate outside the limits, retain the preceding command near either limit, and deactivate within the inclusive inner band.
misleading_near_matches: Turn the alarm off whenever temperature is within the alarm range.
Hold the alarm on for one second after crossing the threshold.
Enable hysteresis only when the temperature status is Valid.

semantic_roles.actor: The command-producing alarm thread; upstream components provide thresholds and mode.
semantic_roles.condition: Current mode and sampled temperature's exact membership in the activation, hold, or reset intervals.
semantic_roles.effect: Emit On, emit Off, or preserve the previous emitted command.
semantic_roles.modality: Required conditional guarantees for each applicable dispatch.
semantic_roles.quantification: Every dispatch satisfying a guard; every reachable previous command.
semantic_roles.temporal_scope: Initialization and discrete compute dispatches, with history from the preceding dispatch; no continuous-time latency claim.
semantic_roles.state_dependency: Hold cases depend on pre-dispatch history; history updates after command computation.
semantic_roles.units_and_boundaries: Shared documented temperature scale and representable arithmetic; strict outer comparisons, closed outer hold endpoints, and inclusive reset endpoints.

record.formal_output_pattern: Abstract mathematical pattern, not executable GUMBO: initialize y=Off and p=Off. For every dispatch t: m=INIT => y=Off; m=FAILED => y=On; (m=NORMAL and (x<L or x>U)) => y=On; (m=NORMAL and ((L<=x and x<L+h) or (U-h<x and x<=U))) => y=p; (m=NORMAL and L+h<=x and x<=U-h) => y=Off. After emitting y, set p_next=y. Interpret all implications conjunctively; map On to the existing source literal Onn.
